oneLine: Anicut-led board offers to buy out key investors in Bira 91.

sources.title: Bira 91 revival plan: Anicut-led board offers to buy out key investors

synopsis: The newly reconstituted board of B9 Beverages, maker of Bira 91, led by Anicut Capital, has offered to acquire the stakes of key investors including Japan's Kirin Holdings, Peak XV Partners, and Belgium's Sofina. This move is part of efforts to recapitalize the financially distressed company and raise fresh funds. Kirin, Peak XV, and Sofina together hold a combined stake of about 41.1%. Incoming investors have set a precondition that existing backers unwilling to join revival efforts must exit before any fresh capital is infused. Kirin Holdings has engaged EY for its stake sale process. The company carries liabilities of 1,000 to 1,500 crore rupees, and its operations have been at a standstill for a year. Former founder Ankur Jain and his family previously gave up their 17.8% stake and board positions to Anicut Capital.
